desc:
The array nxt describes a directed graph on the nodes 0..n-1 in which every node has at most one outgoing edge: nxt[i] is the node that i points to, or -1 if node i has no outgoing edge. A node may point to itself.

A cycle is a set of nodes that can be visited one after another by following the edges and that returns to its first node. Its length is the number of nodes in it (a node that points to itself is a cycle of length 1). Return the length of the longest cycle in the graph, or -1 if there is no cycle.

Example: nxt = [3,3,4,2,3] has the cycle 2 -> 4 -> 3 -> 2 of length 3, so the answer is 3. For [2,-1,3,1] the walk 0 -> 2 -> 3 -> 1 ends at node 1 without edges: -1.
hints: Every node has at most one outgoing edge, so the walk from any node either stops at a node with no edge or runs into a cycle.
Walk from each node that was not seen yet. If the walk reaches a node that belongs to a different, earlier walk, nothing new can be found on this path.

Give every visited node the global time at which it was first reached. During a walk started at time T0, if you reach a node whose stored time is at least T0 then you closed a new cycle, and its length is (current time - stored time).
editorial: Because every node has out-degree at most one, a walk never branches. All nodes of one weakly connected piece funnel into at most one cycle, and every cycle is found by walking from some node that leads into it.

Keep a global counter t and an array seen[u] of the time when u was first visited (or -1). Process each start s that is still unseen: follow edges, assigning seen[u] = t and incrementing t, until you reach -1 or a visited node. If the stopping node v was visited during this very walk (seen[v] ≥ t at start of the walk), the nodes from v to the end of the walk form a cycle of length t - seen[v]. Otherwise v belongs to an earlier walk and its cycle (if any) was already counted. Each node is visited once, so the time is O(n) with O(n) memory. The O(1)-memory alternative applies Floyd's detection from every start, but costs O(n2) in the worst case unless visited nodes are marked.
solution:
def longestCycle(nxt):
    n = len(nxt)
    seen = [-1] * n
    t = 0
    best = -1
    for s in range(n):
        if seen[s] != -1:
            continue
        walk_start = t
        u = s
        while u != -1 and seen[u] == -1:
            seen[u] = t
            t += 1
            u = nxt[u]
        if u != -1 and seen[u] >= walk_start:
            best = max(best, t - seen[u])
    return best
